answer: Because the timber liability is logged in the reef ledger at admission, the quartz audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 34% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind each extra identity it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
